name: Sustainable Materials & Circular Chemistry
tagline: Recyclable materials, bio-based polymers, and circular economy approaches.
seo_title: Sustainable Materials & Circular Chemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Sustainable Materials & Circular Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in recycling, bio-based materials, circular design and resource recovery.

definition.lead: Circular chemistry designs materials and processes so that resources stay in use: made from renewable or recycled feedstocks, and recovered at the end of their life instead of becoming waste.
definition.body: Today most plastics are used once and thrown away. Circular chemistry develops recyclable-by-design polymers, chemical recycling, bio-based feedstocks and ways to recover metals from electronics and batteries.

timeline.title: The recycling symbol
timeline.text: Gary Anderson designs the three-arrow recycling symbol.

timeline.title: Sustainable development
timeline.text: The Brundtland report 'Our Common Future' defines sustainable development.
timeline.why: Meeting today's needs without compromising the future.

timeline.title: Resin codes
timeline.text: Numbered codes are introduced to identify plastic types.

timeline.title: Cradle to Cradle
timeline.text: William McDonough and Michael Braungart publish their book on circular design.
timeline.why: Products designed for endless material cycles.

timeline.title: A plastic-eating bacterium
timeline.text: Japanese researchers report Ideonella sakaiensis, which digests PET.

timeline.title: Plastic's balance sheet
timeline.text: Roland Geyer and colleagues estimate that only about 9% of all plastic ever made was recycled.
timeline.why: Quantified the scale of the problem.

timeline.title: Circular chemistry
timeline.text: Tom Keijer, Vincent Bakker and Chris Slootweg propose principles of circular chemistry.
timeline.why: Extended green chemistry to full life cycles.

timeline.title: Enzymes recycle PET
timeline.text: An engineered enzyme depolymerizes PET efficiently enough to remake bottles.
timeline.why: Brought enzymatic recycling close to industry.

timeline.title: Toward a plastics treaty
timeline.text: The UN Environment Assembly agrees to negotiate a global treaty on plastic pollution.
timeline.why: Plastic pollution became a global policy issue.
